history.period: 18th century (existing structure); legendary origin in the Mahabharata era
history.summary: TOWN CORRECTION: CSV lists the town as Bhavnagar, but the temple is at Koliyak, approx. 24-26 km east of Bhavnagar city, about a kilometre into the Arabian Sea. The temple stands on a small islet off Koliyak beach and is submerged during high tide; it is accessible on foot across the seabed only during low tide (twice daily), when all that is visible at high tide - the flag and pillar - gives way to the shrine. The open platform holds five swayambhu Shiva lingams, each with a Nandi facing it, representing one of the five Pandavas. Legend: after the Kurukshetra war the Pandavas, guilt-stricken at the slaughter of their kin, were told by Krishna to follow a black flag and a black cow until both turned white; at Koliyak beach they did, and the Pandavas meditated and received forgiveness from Shiva, who appeared in lingam form to each brother - hence 'Nishkalank' (spotless, guiltless). Wikipedia credits the existing structure to the 18th century under the Bhavnagar ruler, naming 'Bhavsinhji Takhtasinhji' (attribution uncertain - verify). Managed by a local trust; large gatherings on Maha Shivratri, Navaratri and the Bhadarvi Amavasya fair. Coordinates from datagemba listing of the temple; the islet itself is at sea so coordinates are approximate (verify).

name: Nishkalank Mahadev Temple
town_description: Koliyak is a small coastal village in Bhavnagar district, about 24 km from Bhavnagar city, on the western shore of the Gulf of Khambhat. It is best known for the Nishkalank Mahadev sea temple, one of India's rarest tidal temples, which draws large crowds especially on the Bhadarvi Amavasya fair. The area is quiet and away from the city, with Koliyak beach as the starting point for the walk to the shrine at low tide.

travel.airport: Bhavnagar Airport, approx. 25-30 km by road (verify); Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport, Ahmedabad, approx. 200 km.
travel.railway: Bhavnagar Terminus, approx. 24-28 km; onward by taxi or bus to Koliyak (verify).
travel.road: Koliyak is approx. 23-26 km from Bhavnagar city; buses and taxis run from Bhavnagar to Koliyak (verify). Final access to the temple is a ~1 km walk across the seabed, possible only around low tide.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for comfortable weather; the Bhadarvi Amavasya fair (August-September) is the most important pilgrimage day. Always check the local tide schedule before going, since darshan is possible only around low tide.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported approx. 5:00 AM to 6:00 PM daily (verify - conflicting reports); actual visit windows are governed by the low-tide schedule, so confirm locally on the day. Darshan is free; the final 1 km stretch is a walk over wet sand/mud, so wear suitable footwear.
